Yes, we should control for `risk_score`, although randomization doesn't require it.

Because the email was randomly assigned, the treatment is independent of `risk_score`. A simple difference in means therefore already gives an unbiased estimate of the ATE, and no control is needed to remove confounding.

`risk_score` was measured before the email went out, so it can't be affected by the treatment. It is also likely to predict `payments`. Adding it to the regression soaks up variation in payments that has nothing to do with the email. That shrinks the standard error and gives a tighter estimate of the same effect, without adding bias.

This applies only to pre-treatment variables like `risk_score` and `credit_limit`. Post-treatment variables such as `opened` and `agreement` should not be controlled for, because they would bias the estimate.

I answered from the study design and did not run any regression on the data.

ANSWER: yes
